readings.title: A Weekend of Plans
readings.text:
Selin had expected a quiet weekend, but several plans appeared at once. On Friday evening, she went out with a friend who was preparing for a family celebration. They looked at photographs of different dresses and talked to the shop assistant about colours, sizes and delivery dates. Selin’s friend did not want to buy something she would wear only once, so she chose a simple dress that could be used again.

On Saturday morning, Selin spent time on a clinic project. The team had recently lost one member, and everyone needed to reorganise the work. Selin listened to the project manager, wrote down the new responsibilities and waited for two colleagues to send important files. Although the situation was stressful, the meeting became more positive when everyone offered a practical solution.

That evening, Selin visited relatives and heard stories about weddings, travel and surprising family traditions. One cousin described an old house that people believed was haunted. Selin did not completely believe the story, but she enjoyed the atmosphere and asked several questions. On Sunday she finally had time to rest. Looking back, she realised that a busy weekend can still feel meaningful when work, friendship and family are balanced.

questions.q: Why did the friend choose a simple dress?
What problem did the clinic team have?
What did Selin do in the meeting?
How did Selin feel about the old-house story?

opt: Balance can make a busy weekend meaningful.
